A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoVoc3D and contain five complete, readable pages, including references. Neither contains an appendix. Textual and visual inspection supports comparison of all scientific content.

before.justification: v1 reports original AutoVoc3D evaluation results on nuScenes in Tables 1–2 and qualitative segmentation outputs in Figures 1 and 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original AutoVoc3D quantitative results in Tables 1–2 and qualitative segmentation outputs in Figures 1 and 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same pipeline: generate queries with AutoSeg, merge and deduplicate them, and segment LiDAR points using distilled OpenScene weights.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same auto-vocabulary LiDAR segmentation task on nuScenes. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LidarMultiNet, MinkowskiNet, MSeg Voting, and OpenScene as comparators. Table 2 retains the same OpenScene comparison.

E3.justification: Both versions use the nuScenes validation set, LAVE category mapping for mIoU and mAcc, and TPSS evaluation. Sections 4–5 report identical evaluation procedures and settings.

E4.justification: Figures 1 and 3 retain identical qualitative comparisons with human annotations and OpenScene. Neither version includes additional ablations, sensitivity analyses, or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. AutoVoc3D retains 30.6 mIoU and 44.1 mAcc in Table 1; Table 2 retains TPSS scores of 8.71 for OpenScene and 9.26 for AutoVoc3D.

T1.justification: The problem definition in Section 3.1 and the assumptions, label-assignment rule, and TPSS definition in Section 4.3, including Equations 1–5, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about automatic vocabulary generation, LiDAR segmentation, TPSS, and competitive accuracy without additional training.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of semantic precision and the same qualifications concerning language ambiguity, LAVE discarding novel categories, and TPSS requiring CLIP-aligned point features.

D1.justification: The disclosed components, distilled OpenScene weights, Llama 2 7B evaluator, and resource link are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 25 references are identical. Positioning relative to open-vocabulary segmentation, AutoSeg, and prior auto-vocabulary work is unchanged.

P1.justification: The author name 'Fatemeh Karimi Najadasl' becomes 'Fatemeh Karimi Nejadasl', and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. All other extracted text and the document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Tables 1–2, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–5 render identically; page 1 differs only in the author-name and version/date text covered under P1.

improvement.justification: The revision changes an author's name spelling and the version/date stamp while preserving all scientific content, evidence, explanations, and visual presentation. These limited administrative edits do not establish a meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
